title: Conormal coordinate basis and canonical polynomial comparison for a regular affine ideal
statement: Let $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $U$ an affine open of $V$, and $x_1,\ldots,x_d\in B=\Gamma(U)$ a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] generating its section ideal $I$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. For the fixed conormal presentation [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], there are lifts of the $x_j$ to sections of the first power sheaf whose representatives form a basis of the first graded piece over $\Gamma(s^{-1}U)$. This conormal module is free of rank $d$ on that inverse image, and the canonical symmetric comparison is bijective on sections there. Each basis monomial maps to the homogeneous class represented by the actual corresponding coordinate product in the appropriate ideal power.

source.place: Local construction, centred coordinates and regular-coordinate algebra; old item Steps 1–2. Stacks 054L/lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space, 024T/proposition-properties-sections, 067U/lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion.

proof.text: For I=(x), the generator classes span I/I squared. To prove independence, lift a linear relation over B/I to coefficients in B. Its degree-one polynomial evaluates into I squared. The homogeneous-relation coefficient theorem [lem-pur-regular-sequence-higher-homogeneous-relations] implies that each coefficient belongs to I, so every quotient coefficient vanishes. This constructs the actual basis consisting of generator classes.

Identify B/I with sections of the closed subscheme by the section ring map. The affine conormal sections equivalence in the adopted source, together with the degree-one presentation [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], transports the basis to sections of the conormal piece and identifies each basis vector with the representative of an actual lift of x_j. The affine frame theorem [lem-sc-affine-conormal-frame] gives the free sheaf frame.

Quasi-coherent symmetric-algebra comparison [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine] and the basis polynomial equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] identify the source sections with (B/I)[T_j]. The conormal affine presentation identifies the target with gr_I B. The canonical symmetric comparison agrees on scalars and variables with the regular-sequence polynomial map [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], hence on all polynomials. That map is bijective, as are both presentation isomorphisms, so the canonical comparison is bijective on sections.

Induct additively on the exponent vector to identify the image of each polynomial monomial with its homogeneous associated-graded class. Lift the actual coordinate product from the ideal power to the fixed power sheaf, using the presentation power identification. The affine conormal comparison and the polynomial map equality give precisely the requested monomial formula, including degree zero and the empty index set.

theorem regular_ideal_conormal_coordinates {V S : Scheme.{u}}
    (s : S ⟶ V) [IsClosedImmersion s] (U : V.affineOpens) (d : ℕ)
    (x : Fin d → Γ(V, U.1))
    (hI : Ideal.span (Set.range x) = s.ker.ideal U)
    (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular Γ(V, U.1) (List.ofFn x)) :
    ∃ (coordinateLift : Fin d → (ConormalGradedAlgebra.power s 1).val.obj (op U.1))
      (conormalBasis : Module.Basis (Fin d) Γ(S, s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
    ((ConormalGradedAlgebra.piece s 1).val.obj (op (s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))),
      (∀ j : Fin d,
    (ConormalGradedAlgebra.powerInclusion s 1).val.app (op U.1) (coordinateLift j) = x j) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin d,
    conormalBasis j = ConormalGradedAlgebra.representative s 1 U.1 (coordinateLift j)) ∧
      (∀ α : Fin d →₀ ℕ,
    ∃ a : (ConormalGradedAlgebra.power s α.degree).val.obj (op U.1),
      (ConormalGradedAlgebra.powerInclusion s α.degree).val.app (op U.1) a =
          α.prod (fun j k ↦ x j ^ k) ∧
      (ConormalGradedAlgebra.symmetricComparison s).right.hom.app (op (s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))
          (α.prod (fun j k ↦
            (@id ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.algebra (ConormalGradedAlgebra.piece s 1)).right.obj.obj
              (op (s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))
              ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.inclusion (ConormalGradedAlgebra.piece s 1)).val.app
                (op (s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)) (conormalBasis j))) ^ k)) =
        ConormalGradedAlgebra.homogeneousClass s
          (ConormalGradedAlgebra.presentation s).algebra
          (ConormalGradedAlgebra.presentation s).inclusion α.degree U.1 a) ∧
      Nonempty ((piece s 1).over (s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ≅
        SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin d))) ∧
      Function.Bijective ((symmetricComparison s).right.hom.app (op (s ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))
